id: title:Gilbert09:give up on a repartition that restarts every attempt

review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion recovery and budget protection
review.reason: Adds bounded recovery capability to warehouse ingestion: P1.F1.H1 and P1.F3.H3 change the recovery decision from a naive row-count check to a checkpoint-aware check, while P1.F1.H2 propagates checkpoint state. This could prevent repeated budget burns and allow recovery without restarting from row 0. The chunk lacks complete implementation and test setup, so tier 3 is not supported.
review.uncertainty: Chunk does not include complete implementation and recovery behavior, so tier 3 is not supported.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the complete implementation of the new `RepartitionBudgetExceededError.__init__` and the complete body of `_handle_budget_exceeded` and the test setup, so while the change is described and the test assertions are visible, the actual execution and recovery behavior is not fully demonstrated. observations.behavior: Adds a new parameter `resumed_from` to the exception and its assignment, and its use in the recovery decision. The change is bounded to warehouse ingestion and recovery.
observations.posthog_connection: This parameter distinguishes whether an attempt inherited rows from a checkpoint or started fresh, which is used to distinguish convergence from a treadmill. This could prevent repeated budget burns and allow recovery without restarting from row 0.

observations.behavior: Passes the inherited row count into the exception when the rewrite exceeds its activity budget.
observations.posthog_connection: This connects the checkpoint state to the recovery decision, allowing the caller to distinguish between an attempt that inherited rows and one that did not.

observations.behavior: Changes the recovery decision from `rows_written > 0` to `resumed_from > 0 and rows_written > 0`. This could prevent false positives where an attempt that inherited nothing and wrote many rows is treated as progress.
observations.posthog_connection: This could prevent repeated budget burns and allow recovery without restarting from row 0.
